product_relevance.what_product_question_it_informs: How many names carry a particular DNS configuration, as a very indirect infrastructure signal.
product_relevance.weakest_truthful_interpretation: A count of names whose published DNS records have a stated property. It is a fact about DNS configuration and nothing else.
product_relevance.why_weak: The tempting reading — that a name pointing at a provider indicates a customer of that provider — is exactly the semantic promotion §6 C4 and §7 forbid. Stripped of it, the proposition is about zone contents.

proposition.population: a defined set of domain names
proposition.predicate: the name resolved to a record with the stated property
proposition.exclusion_rule: names outside the defined set are outside the frame
proposition.configuration_assumptions: the same name set on both sides

what_a_positive_observation_establishes: That a name resolved to a record with a property at a moment, from that resolver.
explicit_non_claims: not that the domain's owner is a customer of anyone
not adoption, spend or market share
not comparable with any IP-population measurement

population_incomparability.$comment: §10 and §13. Recorded because this is where the mistake would be made.
population_incomparability.statement: This construct's population is DOMAIN_NAME. It may never be compared with, combined with, or substituted for an IP_ADDRESS population, and a count of names is not a count of addresses.

Netlas.note: Domain data is collected; the observation semantics for a DNS proposition were not resolved.

Rapid7 Project Sonar.note: Forward and reverse DNS studies exist as dated files, described as DNS responses for known forward DNS names and IPv4 PTR responses.
